surprises.description: Q4 EPS was far below the preview’s $0.80 consensus: Greenbrier reported $0.27, or $0.39 excluding $0.12 per share of facility-related rationalization costs. Even the adjusted figure was about half the expected amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue was $591 million ... with EPS of $0.27, or $0.39 excluding $0.12 per share of facility-related rationalization costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS ... Consensus $0.80”; the preview also said the practical bar was “mid-to-high $0.80s.”

surprises.description: Greenbrier’s FY2027 EPS guidance has a lower bound below the preview’s roughly $3.35 market-implied figure, although the upper bound is higher. The $2.75–$3.75 range therefore leaves more downside at the low end than the preview’s “guide starting with a 3” expectation suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For fiscal 2027, Greenbrier guided to EPS of $2.75 to $3.75.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 11.4x forward multiple implies a market FY27 EPS near ~$3.35”; “A guide starting with a 3 is survivable.”

surprises.description: Full-year deliveries came in below the FY26 guidance range, rather than reaching the expected 15,650–15,850 cars. Greenbrier delivered 15,400, a shortfall of 250–450 cars.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Greenbrier delivered 15,400 railcars in fiscal 2026,” with results “falling below company expectations for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 guidance of “15,650–15,850” deliveries.

surprises.description: FY26 core EPS was below the company’s guidance range: $2.60 versus the preview’s cited $3.00–$3.15 guide. This adds a full-year shortfall beyond the Q4 miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Greenbrier delivered ... core EPS of $2.60,” with results “falling below company expectations for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s FY26 guidance table listed diluted EPS of “$3.00–3.15.”

surprises.description: FY26 aggregate gross margin was below the bottom of the cited full-year guidance range. The reported 13.6% compares with expected guidance of 13.8%–14.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aggregate gross margin of 13.6%,” with results “falling below company expectations for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 aggregate gross margin guidance of “13.8–14.2%.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue missed the $605.1 million consensus, although it remained within the $530–$630 million range implied by FY26 guidance. The miss was modest at about 2%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ... Consensus $605.1M”; the preview’s guidance-implied Q4 range was “$530–630M.”

surprises.description: Backlog and book-to-bill were stronger than the preview’s estimate: backlog rose to 14,000 cars and $2.1 billion, and Q4 book-to-bill was near 1. The preview expected roughly 13,150–13,350 cars, about $2.0 billion, and a Q4 book-to-bill around 0.86x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog rose to 14,000 railcars valued at $2.1 billion, the first sequential increase since fiscal 2024”; Q4 book-to-bill was “near 1, the highest since Q3 fiscal 2024.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bridge estimated “13,150–13,350 units, ~$2.0B” and “Q4 book-to-bill ≈ 0.86x.”

surprises.description: Recurring revenue grew substantially as Greenbrier expanded its owned fleet, providing a stronger leasing contribution than the preview quantified. The preview flagged leasing earnings as a possible offset to manufacturing weakness; the reported recurring-revenue increase was 55%.
surprises.fact_evidence: The owned lease fleet grew “by roughly 4,000 railcars (23%) to approximately 21,000 units” at “98% utilization,” while recurring revenue “grew 55% to $175 million from $113 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “whether recurring leasing earnings keep backfilling manufacturing weakness.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that pending trade actions are weighing on tank-car demand, a risk the preview did not identify. Management tempered the concern, saying the actions would raise prices passed to customers and would not materially affect Greenbrier’s long-term financial performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pending trade actions on tank cars and freight rail couplers are weighing on tank car demand,” but management said they “would raise prices passed to customers without materially impacting Greenbrier's long-term financial performance.”
